sources_considered.why: Salesforce AI Research benchmark of LLM agents on business tasks, May 2025.
CMU TheAgentCompany benchmark, version 2 from May 2025.
Counterweight: shows agent reliability improving fast over time.

receipt.public_excerpt: even leading LLM agents achieve modest overall success rates on CRMArena-Pro, typically around 58% in single-turn scenarios, with performance significantly degrading to approximately 35% in multi-turn settings.

evidence_items.explanation: In mid-2025 the leading LLM agents failed most multi-turn business tasks. That is not robust, trustworthy performance.

receipt.public_excerpt: in a setting simulating a real workplace, a good portion of simpler tasks could be solved autonomously, but more difficult long-horizon tasks are still beyond the reach of current systems.

evidence_items.explanation: In this version the best agent completed only about 30% of workplace tasks. Long-horizon tasks were beyond current systems.

receipt.public_excerpt: We also measure the 80% time horizon of models (Figure 6) and find a similar trend, though horizons are roughly 5x shorter.

evidence_items.explanation: Agents were far less capable at high reliability than at 50% reliability. But reliability was improving steadily, which bears on the forward-looking reading Marcus may have intended.

unresolved_gaps: Whether continued LLM progress will eventually yield robust, trustworthy agents cannot be settled from evidence before the post.
